edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Μηδεὶς πλανάσθω: καὶ τὰ ἐπουράνια καὶ ἡ δόξα τῶν ἀγγέλων καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες ὁρατοί τε καὶ ἀόρατοι, ἐὰν μὴ πιστεύσωσιν εἰς τὸ αἷμα Χριστοῦ, κἀκείνοις κρίσις ἐστίν: ὁ χωρῶν χωρείτω. τόπος μηδένα φυσιούτω: τὸ γὰρ ὅλον ἐστὶν πίστις καὶ ἀγάπη, ὧν οὐδὲν προκέκριται. [2] καταμάθετε δὲ τοὺς ἑτεροδοξοῦντας εἰς τὴν χάριν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τὴν εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐλθοῦσαν, πῶς ἐναντίοι εἰσὶν τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ. περὶ ἀγάπης οὐ μέλει αὐτοῖς, οὐ περὶ χήρας, οὐ περὶ ὀρφανοῦ, οὐ περὶ θλιβομένου, οὐ περὶ δεδεμένου ἢ λελυμένου, οὐ περὶ πεινῶντος ἢ διψῶντος.
pass_a_gloss: [1] Let no one be deceived. Even the heavenly beings and the glory of the angels and the rulers, both visible and invisible, if they do not believe in the blood of Christ, for them too there is judgment. Let the one who can make room for it make room for it. Let position puff no one up; for the whole thing is faith and love, and nothing is preferred before them. [2] But take note of those who hold different opinions about the grace of Jesus Christ that came to us, how opposed they are to the mind of God. They have no concern for love, none for the widow, none for the orphan, none for the oppressed, none for the one in chains or the one set free, none for the hungry or thirsty.
pass_b_english: Let no one be deceived. Even the beings of heaven, the glory of the angels, and the rulers seen and unseen (Colossians 1:16), if they do not believe in the blood of Christ, face judgment too. Let anyone who can accept this accept it (Matthew 19:12). Let no one be puffed up by rank. Faith and love are everything. Nothing is preferred to them.

Take note of those who hold other opinions about the grace of Jesus Christ that has come to us, and see how opposed they are to the mind of God. They have no concern for love. They do not care for the widow or the orphan or the oppressed, for the prisoner or the freed, for the hungry or the thirsty.

choices.why: τόπος here is position or office in the church, not physical place.
rejected: let not place puff anyone up (opaque)

choices.why: 'Hold other opinions' is the verb's sense; avoids the later technical 'heterodox' and does not add 'teach'.
Paired participles kept as a pair.

'visible and invisible ... rulers' echoes Paul's list of created powers; allusion, not quotation.

Repair 2026-10-02 (round 2): third-person imperatives kept ('Let no one be deceived', 'Let no one be puffed up'); 'teach' and the reflexive 'set themselves against' removed; ἐναντίοι εἰσίν rendered 'how opposed they are'.

review.notes: Paragraph [1] checked in full (internal sections 1 and 2). Pass A keeps clause sense: 'Let no one be deceived' for 'Μηδεὶς πλανάσθω', 'for them too there is judgment' for 'κἀκείνοις κρίσις ἐστίν', and 'how opposed they are to the mind of God' for 'πῶς ἐναντίοι εἰσὶν τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ'. Pass B does not: 'Make no mistake' replaces the third-person deception jussive, and 'See how they set themselves against the mind of God' adds reflexive agency. 'those who teach otherwise about the grace' adds teaching beyond 'τοὺς ἑτεροδοξοῦντας εἰς τὴν χάριν' and Pass A 'those who hold different opinions about the grace'. Dropped γάρ/δέ and the compressed οὐ-περὶ list in B were treated as style, not omitted arguments. Inline (Matthew 19:12) and (Colossians 1:16) match the supplied allusion notes; adding them is not a fault. Title 'Faith and Love Are Everything' names τὸ ὅλον ἐστὶν πίστις καὶ ἀγάπη, not only the locus.
reasons: Pass B 'Make no mistake. Even the beings of heaven' does not preserve 'Μηδεὶς πλανάσθω: καὶ τὰ ἐπουράνια' or Pass A 'Let no one be deceived. Even the heavenly beings': the Greek is a third-person passive jussive that no one be led astray, not a second-person assurance.
Pass B 'See how they set themselves against the mind of God' adds reflexive agency absent from 'πῶς ἐναντίοι εἰσὶν τῇ γνώμῃ τοῦ θεοῦ' and from Pass A 'how opposed they are to the mind of God.'
Pass B 'those who teach otherwise about the grace' adds teaching not in 'τοὺς ἑτεροδοξοῦντας εἰς τὴν χάριν' or Pass A 'those who hold different opinions about the grace'.

review.notes: Source identity: Greek text matches Ignatius, Smyrnaeans 6 (Lake 1912 Loeb). Completeness: all clauses, arguments, repetitions, qualifications, and quotations from the single Greek paragraph are present in both Pass A and Pass B. Negation: μηδεὶς πλanasθω correctly rendered as 'Let no one be deceived' / 'Make no mistake'; ἐὰν μὴ πιστεύσωσιν as 'if they do not believe'. Agency: subjects and actions preserved (heavenly beings, rulers, those who hold different opinions). Modality: ἐὰν μὴ preserved as conditional 'if they do not believe'; χωρείτω as imperative 'let the one who can make room'. Doctrine: faithful to Ignatius's anti-docetic emphasis on blood of Christ and faith/love as sole criteria. Scripture: Pass B adds inline citations (Colossians 1:16, Matthew 19:12) as allusion/verbal echo per notes; these are additions, not contradictions, and Pass A lacks them but does not contradict. Title 'Faith and Love Are Everything' names the thought, not just locus. Notes disclose OCR damage and uncertain readings via variants empty and witness note. No failures in any check; covered_source_paragraphs: [1]; no uncertainties or reasons.
